title: Holiday Party Planning Kit
subtitle: Office and home holiday parties, from Friendsgiving through New Year's, with Chicago winter logistics
intro: December is the busiest month for event bookings in the Chicago area, and the weather adds its own challenges. This kit helps you lock in a date early, plan food and drinks, and handle coats, snow, and parking so the party feels easy for your guests.

sections.heading: Planning Timeline
sections.note: For parties between Thanksgiving and New Year's, start in September or early October.

tasks: Decide the type of party: office party, family gathering, Friendsgiving, neighborhood open house, or New Year's Eve.
Pick two or three possible dates and avoid the busiest weekends if you can, such as the first and second Saturdays in December.
Set a total budget and a per-guest target.
Reserve a venue, restaurant room, or banquet space, or confirm your home hosting plan.
Request quotes for rentals now, since tables, chairs, linens, and glassware book up in December.
Book caterers, bartenders, or a food truck before their calendars fill.
Create the guest list and note plus-ones, kids, and dietary needs.
Send a save-the-date by email or text.
Choose a theme: classic, cozy, winter white, glam, or ugly sweater.
Book DJ, live music, or plan a playlist.
Plan photo moments such as a backdrop or photo booth.
Ask a friend or coworker to join a small planning committee.
Send formal invitations with an RSVP deadline.
Finalize the menu and drink list with your caterer or shopping plan.
Order rentals: chairs, tables, linens, dinnerware, glassware, and lounge furniture.
Plan decor and order lights, centerpieces, and table decor.
Plan a gift exchange or white elephant if you want one.
Check office policies on alcohol, hours, and guests.
Follow up on RSVPs and update your headcount.
Plan coat check or a coat rack area, and boot trays for snowy days.
Plan parking: street, lot, valet, or rideshare drop-off.
Confirm rental delivery and pickup windows.
Confirm vendors' arrival times and menus.
Buy nonalcoholic drinks, ice, and paper goods if self-catering.
Give the final headcount to the caterer and rental company.
Check the forecast and plan for snow removal, salt, and shoveled paths.
Do a walk-through of the space and plan where coats, food, and drinks will go.
Prep make-ahead dishes and label them.
Send a reminder to guests with address, parking, and start time.
Charge speakers and test lights and music.
Set up tables and chairs at least 2 hours before guests arrive.
Salt the entrance and keep a mat and towels at the door.
Put out food in stages and refresh as needed.
Arrange safe rides home for guests who need them.
Return or ready rentals for pickup.
Send thank-you messages and share photos.

groups.title: Office party
items: Confirm budget and approval with leadership or HR.
Choose a time that works for different shifts or remote teams.
Plan inclusive food, drinks, and activities for all backgrounds.
Offer nonalcoholic options and clear end times.
Arrange for a gift exchange or recognition moment if appropriate.
Plan rides home or transit information.
Collect dietary needs by survey before ordering food.

groups.title: Home holiday party
items: Set a guest limit based on your space and fire safety.
Plan coat storage, such as a bed or a rack.
Clear walkways and add runners for wet floors.
Set up a drink station away from the kitchen.
Plan trash and recycling bins.
Let neighbors know about the party and parking.
Move fragile decor and breakables out of walkways.
Check that smoke alarms work and exits are clear.

groups.title: Friendsgiving and Thanksgiving
items: Pick the date, often the weekend before or after Thanksgiving Day.
Assign dishes so you do not end up with five pies.
Rent extra tables and chairs for a longer table.
Plan for vegetarian and allergy-friendly options.
Keep the oven and stovetop schedule on a sheet.
Ask guests to bring their own containers for leftovers.
Borrow or rent a second oven-safe warmer or chafing dishes.

groups.title: New Year's Eve
items: Plan the midnight toast and glassware.
Provide nonalcoholic sparkling options.
Arrange safe transport and overnight options.
Set up a countdown clock or screen.
Plan late-night snacks.
Prepare a cleanup plan for the morning after.
Set a clear plan for sleeping arrangements or rides before the first drink.

sections.heading: Winter Logistics Checklist
sections.note: Chicago winters are unpredictable. A little planning keeps guests warm and safe.

groups.title: Coats and entry
items: Set up a coat rack or coat check with numbered tickets.
Place boot trays and mats at the door.
Provide a towel station for wet shoes.
Have a place for umbrellas and hats.
Assign a helper to greet guests and take coats.

groups.title: Snow and parking
items: Shovel and salt the walkway before guests arrive.
Check city parking rules, including winter overnight bans and snow routes.
Share rideshare drop-off instructions and an alternate parking option.
Add a snow date or a flexible start time if the forecast is severe.
Light the entrance and path clearly after dark.
Keep a shovel and salt near the door in case of a late snowfall.

groups.title: Heat and comfort
items: Check the heating system a week before the party.
Plan for crowd warmth, since packed rooms heat up fast.
Add extra seating for older guests.
If using a tent, ask about heaters and sidewalls.
Plan warm drinks such as cider, cocoa, and coffee.
Keep a first aid kit and basic medicines nearby.

groups.title: Booking crunch
items: Call venues and rental companies as early as September for December dates.
Ask caterers whether December has minimums or higher rates.
Book rideshare codes, shuttles, or a valet before the busiest weekends.
Have a backup date or a smaller-version plan if a vendor cancels.
Order decor, lights, and supplies early to avoid shipping delays.

sections.heading: Food and Drink Amounts
sections.note: Rough guidelines for a 3 to 4 hour party. Adjust based on whether you serve a meal or appetizers.

sections.heading: Budget Split
sections.note: Rough starting shares. Office budgets often have a fixed per-person cap.

lines.tip: Heavy appetizers and stations can be a lower-cost alternative to a plated dinner.
A signature cocktail plus beer and wine reduces cost.
Weeknight and daytime dates are often more affordable than weekend nights.
Book early, since December inventory moves fast.
String lights, greenery, and candles can have a big impact at a small cost.
A good playlist and speaker can work for smaller parties.

lines.category: Staffing, coat check, and parking help
lines.tip: Even one helper at the door makes arrival smoother.
Set aside a little for extra ice, salt, or last-minute needs.

sections.heading: Tips for a Smooth Holiday Party
items: Book your venue and rentals before Halloween if you can. December weekends are the first to fill.
Pick an off-peak date such as a weeknight or an early December weekend for better availability.
Put a snack or small bite out early so guests are not hungry while they wait for dinner.
Make a quiet corner for guests who want a break from the noise.
Place drinks in more than one location to avoid lines.
Add a nonalcoholic option that feels festive, like a cider or a mocktail.
Plan for the unexpected with extra chairs, ice, and napkins.
Ask a friend to be the cleanup captain so you can enjoy the party.
